payload.name: Verify explicit event timing evidence
payload.description: When a question asks when an event happened (finished, completed, started), require evidence that explicitly states that event's timing; do not substitute a related event's date (publication, exhibit, announcement).
content: When a question asks when an event happened (finished, completed, started, created), verify the cited memory explicitly describes that event and its timing. Do not answer with the date of a related event (publication, exhibition, announcement) unless a memory explicitly equates that date with the requested event's time.

If retrieved memories only concern related events or lack explicit timing for the requested event, judge the evidence insufficient and run additional searches using temporal/completion phrases (e.g., 'completed', 'finished', 'a few days ago', 'recently') and structured filters on the relevant subject/predicate (e.g., artwork/created/completed).

When a search returns a memory with explicit relative timing (e.g., 'a few days ago'), resolve the date from the memory/session timestamp and cite that memory as evidence rather than the related-event memory.

solves: Questions asking when a specific event happened (completion, finish, start) fail when the agent uses a related event's date (publication, exhibition, announcement) or answers without explicit timing evidence. The rule requires explicit temporal evidence for the requested event and adds completion-focused supplementary searches, applying to any 'when did X finish/complete Y' question across topics.
